howto.name: Meet the basic requirements
howto.text: Be at least 18 with a high school diploma or equivalent and a U.S. Social Security number.

howto.name: Complete the 63-hour pre-license course
howto.text: Finish Florida's state-approved 63-hour sales associate pre-license course and pass its end-of-course exam.

howto.name: Get fingerprinted
howto.text: Submit electronic fingerprints through a state-approved vendor for your background check.

howto.name: Apply to the DBPR
howto.text: Apply to the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation and receive your exam authorization.

howto.name: Pass the Florida state exam
howto.text: Pass the 100-question Florida sales associate exam (75% or higher) at a Pearson VUE testing center.

howto.name: Activate your license under a broker
howto.text: Join a licensed Florida broker, such as Adams, Cameron & Co.'s Ormond Beach office, to activate your license and start working.

Ormond Beach is one of the most established and sought-after communities in Volusia County — which makes it a strong place to build a real estate career. Here’s exactly how to get licensed, and what the local market looks like for a new agent.

How do you get a real estate license in Ormond Beach?

You earn a Florida real estate sales associate license, which is valid statewide — there’s no separate Ormond Beach license. The steps: be 18+ with a high school diploma, complete the 63-hour pre-license course, get fingerprinted, apply to the DBPR, pass the state exam (75% to pass), and activate your license under a broker. Most people finish in two to four months. Full detail is in our Florida licensing guide.

Is Ormond Beach a good market for a new real estate agent?

Yes — in a different way than a boomtown. Ormond Beach is established and desirable, with a mix of beachside properties on the barrier island and family neighborhoods on the mainland along the Granada Boulevard corridor. It draws steady relocation and second-home interest. Across Volusia County, roughly 900 homes sell each month at about a $343,000 median, and inventory has risen, giving newer agents more listings to work and sellers who need representation. It’s a relationship market, which rewards an agent who knows the area and stays visible.

Does the brokerage you start with matter?

More than the town you pick. Your license must be held by a broker, and that brokerage decides your training, tools, and support in the make-or-break first year. In an established market like Ormond Beach, a recognized local name carries real weight — sellers trust it before you say a word.

Adams, Cameron & Co. has been the area’s largest brokerage since 1963, with an office right on West Granada Boulevard in Ormond Beach and around 300 agents across Volusia and Flagler County. New agents get in-house marketing at no cost, seven-day non-competing manager support, structured training, and the global Leading Real Estate Companies of the World referral network. That’s the difference between a desk and a real start.

Read the licensing guide, then start a conversation with the Adams, Cameron & Co. Ormond Beach office. No pressure — just a clear picture of the path.
